page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on x86_64 Intel Xeon processors operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. It features 2 vCPUs allocated across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core via Hyper-Threading. The system is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. The CPU features support for instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AES encryption, BMI2, and FMA. There are no GPUs or local NVMe storage drives bundled with this instance type.

In synthetic and practical benchmark assessments, the n2-standard-2 instance demonstrates entry-level performance metrics. The stress-ng multi-core CPU score reaches 1837.38, while the single-core benchmark achieves 1398.19. Single-core processing metrics in Geekbench register a score of 1123.0, alongside a multi-core score of 1333.0. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth tests show read rates of 13.8 GB/sec and write rates of 11.79 GB/sec. Despite lower multi-core compute throughput, single-threaded gzip compression yields a processing speed of 23.81 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput registers at 1.95 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations handle 1.72 million operations per second.

Featuring dedicated CPU resources rather than burstable credit allocation, the n2-standard-2 provides consistent baseline processing capacity without CPU throttling risks. Its 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio offers standard density for lightweight software deployments. Given the low total multi-core compute headroom and modest memory bandwidth, this server configuration is best suited for small-scale web serving, light utility microservices, staging environments, basic API endpoints, and low-volume caching tasks.
